record.summary: Voluntary, non-binding guidance from Qatar's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology for developers and deployers of AI systems that affect the public. It sets eight principles: do no harm; ensure robustness, security and safety; avoid perpetuating bias and discrimination; protect the environment; safeguard privacy; promote transparency; develop a human-centred approach; and assign ultimate accountability to humans. It calls for risk evaluations before deployment, robustness testing, continuous monitoring, discrimination impact assessments, bias audits, human intervention and appeal for consequential decisions, and external audits of systems that inform significant decisions.
record.notes: Posted on the government e-participation portal Sharek on 16 May 2024 together with the companion 'Artificial Intelligence in Qatar—Principles and Guidelines for Ethical Use', which addresses users of AI systems such as private companies, government agencies, the public and students. Both documents are to be updated every one to two years. The guidelines are aligned with UNESCO and OECD standards and refer to the National Cyber Security Agency's 'Guidelines for Secure Adoption and Usage of Artificial Intelligence' for risk evaluation and security standards.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored: the Sharek forum post on sharek.gov.qa, captured on 11 Oct 2026 with the post text, its date and the titles of the two attached documents, and again on 18 Oct 2026, when the capture held only the page frame and a reader's response without the post text; and the development-and-deployment guidelines PDF (13 pages) from prod16-assets.sprinklr.com, a host pipeline/official-sites.json lists as proposed, so its quotes count as secondary. The 11 Oct capture confirms the title, the 16 May 2024 posting date, the companion document and the non-binding, voluntary nature; the PDF confirms MCIT's authorship, the eight principles and the guidelines. Sharek is a government portal, but no stored file shows that MCIT runs it, so its quotes are labelled alt-official. MCIT's own pages on mcit.gov.qa answered with a maintenance page or HTTP 500 in an earlier run; the AI Committee page, requested again in this run, answered HTTP 403 to the archiver, also in the browser, so it is not stored. Trackers give conflicting dates (2024 issue; 8 May 2025 'effective'), and a Qatar News Agency report of 25 May 2025 describes the documents as recently issued by MCIT; none of these is stored.
